daily_load_assessment: Today you are in an optimal window for high-intensity adaptation. Your CTL sits at 39.0, ATL is at 35.5, leaving you with a positive Training Stress Balance (TSB) of +3.4. Your HRV is stable and balanced at 49 ms. Although no sleep score was recorded, your physiological indicators suggest you are fully recovered from your last light Z2 running session on August 27. You have zero residual muscular or cardiovascular fatigue, meaning you are cleared for high-intensity work today.
acute_status_assessment_3_weeks: Over the last 21 days, you accumulated 14.18 training hours and 936 TSS. This represents a safe and steady volume, but it is heavily skewed toward cycling (8 performance sessions vs. only 3 running sessions). Your running baseline is currently under-stimulated. To hit your 5km running pace and interval quality milestones, we must strategically introduce structured high-intensity running blocks while your acute fatigue (ATL) remains low.
sport_trend_assessment_6_months: Your long-term athletic profile shows an exceptional low-intensity aerobic engine, fortified by your consistent daily e-bike commuting. At a current body weight of 73.0 kg, your 258W FTP translates to a competitive 3.53 W/kg. However, your CTL is plateauing at around 39. To reach your target fitness CTL of 60, we need to implement a progressive ramp rate of +1 to +2 CTL per week. This requires transitioning from passive commuting to structured, sport-specific workouts that challenge your V02max and anaerobic threshold.
coach_verdict: We are executing Priority 1 (VO2max Running Intervals) today. Your positive TSB (+3.4) and balanced HRV (49 ms) present the perfect physiological storm to strike your aerobic capacity. Running has been neglected in your recent 3-week block, and we must build your running economy and VO2max pace immediately if you want to crush that 5km target. No excuses—you are fresh, primed, and the data demands high performance today.

priority_1.workout_details: Warm-up: 15 minutes of progressive Zone 2 running, ending with 3x100m strides. Main Set: 5 x 800 meters at target 5km pace (Zone 5, RPE 9). Rest: 3 minutes of passive walking recovery between intervals to ensure full PCr system replenishment. Cool-down: 10 minutes of easy jogging/walking in Zone 1.
priority_1.reason: Your physiology is fully recovered (TSB +3.4), and running VO2max stimulus is the highest priority gap in your current 21-day training history. This directly targets your 5km pace and interval quality milestones.

priority_2.workout_details: Main Set: 90 minutes of continuous, steady-state Zone 2 cycling on flat to rolling terrain, keeping cadence strict at 90-95 RPM. Post-ride: 3 sets of 15 Heavy Sandbag Get-ups (70kg) and 3x60-second planks for core stability and rotational strength.
priority_2.reason: If you lack the mental focus for high-intensity running today, this option adheres perfectly to the 70/30 Pyramidal rule. It safely drives CTL upward towards your target of 60 by leveraging your robust aerobic cycling base while reinforcing torque capability with the heavy sandbag.

priority_3.session_title: Heavy Lower Body Torque & Upper Aesthetics
priority_3.workout_details: Warm-up: Dynamic mobility, 3x10 Goblet Squats (20kg KB). Main Lift 1: Barbell Back Squat - 4 sets x 5 reps @ 85kg (focus on explosive concentric drive). Main Lift 2: Romanian Deadlift - 3 sets x 8 reps @ 80kg. Accessory 1: Bench Press - 3 sets x 8 reps @ 70kg. Accessory 2: Barbell Bicep Curls - 3 sets x 12 reps. Accessory 3: Hanging Leg Raises - 3 sets x 15 reps.
priority_3.reason: This develops raw neuromuscular recruitment and structural durability. It supports cycling torque (for your 5-min and 20-min power milestones) and provides running injury prevention while satisfying your goals for upper body and core aesthetics.
